parts.article:
Growing more for less
 
Satellite technology is helping farmers boost crop yields
 
A For farmers, working out the optimal amount of seed, fertiliser, pesticide and water to scatter on a field can make, or break, the subsequent harvest. Regular laboratory analyses of soil and plant samples from various parts of the field can help – but such expertise is costly, and often unavailable. However, a new and cheaper method of doing this analysis is now on offer. Precise prescriptions for growing crops can be obtained quickly, and less expensively, by calculating the amount of electromagnetic radiation reflected from agricultural land. The data is collected by orbiting satellites.
 
B Examining the wavelength of the radiation that is reflected can reveal, with surprising precision, the properties of the soil, the quantity of crop being grown, and the levels in those crops of chlorophyll*, various minerals, moisture and other indicators of their quality. If recent and forecast weather data is added to the mix, detailed maps can be produced indicating exactly how, where and when crops should be grown. The service usually costs less than US$15 per hectare for a handful of readings a year, and can increase yields by as much as 10%.
 
C Such precision farming using satellite-based intelligence is a relatively new technique. Even so, it is catching on quickly. Five times a year, for example, a French cereal-growers’ co-operative called Sevépi purchases satellite data and makes it available to its members in the form of maps of their fields, divided into three or four colour-coded zones per hectare. For each zone, one of about 50 fertiliser formulas is recommended. On top of this, if the wheat in the field has already grown quite high early in the season, and heavy showers are expected, an appropriate dose of growth regulator is recommended for each zone. (Long, fragile stems break more easily in downpours.) Then, farm vehicles equipped with global-positioning system locators automatically mix and apply the prescribed dose to each area.
 
D France is the pioneer in this sort of surveillance. More farmland is analysed by satellite there than in any other country, according to Infoterra (a subsidiary of EADS Astrium), the firm that is France’s largest provider of such information, supplying data to companies such as Sevépi. Moreover, Henri Douche, head of Infoterra’s agriculture sales in Toulouse, reckons the amount of monitored farmland will increase as weather patterns change and farmers can no longer rely on the past as a guide to the future. When confounded by the yield variations that these new weather patterns will bring, even farmers who are afraid of new technology will sign up, he says.
 
E Inexpensive data on the productivity of land is advantageous to governments, too. Areas where fertilisers and pesticides are being applied excessively can be pinpointed, studied and regulated by environmental and land-use agencies. Guy Lafond, an agronomist with Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, a government agency, says the satellite data it purchases is proving useful for the study of fields with declining productivity in the province of Saskatchewan. Overkill with nitrate fertilisers (which are also a source of greenhouse gases) appears partly responsible. And according to RapidEye, a German satellite operator, insurance companies are also studying satellite data with a view to selling insurance policies to governments of famine-prone countries that might be threatened by crop failure.
 
F In March, RapidEye began selling data that helps forecast harvests. ‘Too often, farmers limit productivity by managing fields uniformly,’ says Fredrick Jung-Rothenhaüsler, head of product development at the firm’s headquarters in Brandenburg an der Havel. ‘Our satellites are the first commercial satellites to include the Red-Edge band of the light spectrum, which is sensitive to changes in chlorophyll content. More research will be necessary to realise the full potential of the Red-Edge band. However, this band can assist in monitoring vegetation health, improving species separation and also help in measuring protein and nitrogen content in biomass.’ The company’s data, which comes from both Europe and the Americas, breaks field productivity down into patches just five metres square.
 
G The advantages that satellite technology provides in terms of precision farming do not have to be restricted to rich countries. In Africa, where many soils have become badly depleted of nutrients, better fertiliser management would greatly improve the situation. As a consequence, the charitable trust World Agroforestry Centre, in the city of Nairobi, in Kenya, has begun to build up a catalogue of the radiation patterns derived from around 100,000 samples of African soils. The information is the key to understanding the potential of these soils to be more agriculturally productive. Once passed on to the International Centre for Tropical Agriculture, based in Colombia, South America, it is intended that the information be used to build a database called the ‘Digital Soil Map’. When ready, this will provide farmers with free forecasts, developed with regularly updated satellite imagery, across farmland in a number of countries in Africa. This is information which will almost certainly assist in improving crop yields. For a hunger-ravaged continent, that is good news indeed.

questions.question: an example of how farmers in one country are now using satellite data to determine fertiliser use

analyses.content: 你可能会看到 B 段提到了土壤属性和矿物质，但那里只是在讲卫星能检测什么，并没有提到具体哪个国家的农民如何用它来施肥。

[C段] Five times a year, for example, a French cereal-growers' co-operative called Sevépi purchases satellite data and makes it available to its members in the form of maps of their fields, divided into three or four colour-coded zones per hectare. For each zone, one of about 50 fertiliser formulas is recommended.
这一段明确举了法国合作社 Sevépi 购买卫星数据并为每块田推荐 50 种肥料配方之一的例子。

questions.question: a reference to climate change and its effects

analyses.content: 文中提到天气模式正在改变，农民不能再靠过去的经验，这种“天气模式改变”就是对气候变化的直接描述。
不要在文中死找“climate change”这个原词，理解“weather patterns change”和“new weather patterns”带来的产量波动才是关键。

[D段] Moreover, Henri Douche, head of Infoterra's agriculture sales in Toulouse, reckons the amount of monitored farmland will increase as weather patterns change and farmers can no longer rely on the past as a guide to the future. When confounded by the yield variations that these new weather patterns will bring, even farmers who are afraid of new technology will sign up, he says.

questions.question: a reference to the effect on the soil of using too much fertiliser

analyses.content: 这一段点名批评了硝酸盐肥料的“过度使用（Overkill）”是导致加拿大某些地区土地生产力下降的部分原因。
注意“declining productivity”就是化肥用多后对土地产生的负面后果，别只顾着找“soil”这个词。

[E段] Guy Lafond, an agronomist with Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, a government agency, says the satellite data it purchases is proving useful for the study of fields with declining productivity in the province of Saskatchewan. Overkill with nitrate fertilisers (which are also a source of greenhouse gases) appears partly responsible.

questions.question: an example of information that will be shared between different countries

analyses.content: 这一题的关键在于识别文中的地名转换，看到非洲、肯尼亚、哥伦比亚、南美等词的联动，就能锁定“不同国家间共享”。
文中描述了位于肯尼亚（非洲）的机构收集土壤数据，交给位于哥伦比亚（南美）的机构处理，最后服务于多个非洲国家，这就是典型的跨国信息共享。

[G段] As a consequence, the charitable trust World Agroforestry Centre, in the city of Nairobi, in Kenya, has begun to build up a catalogue of the radiation patterns derived from around 100,000 samples of African soils. Once passed on to the International Centre for Tropical Agriculture, based in Colombia, South America, it is intended that the information be used to build a database called the 'Digital Soil Map'. When ready, this will provide farmers with free forecasts, developed with regularly updated satellite imagery, across farmland in a number of countries in Africa.

questions.question: a mention of the country which is the leader in agricultural technology

analyses.content: 开头第一句就直白地说法国是这类监测的“先驱（pioneer）”，且被卫星分析的农田面积超过其他任何国家。
看到“pioneer”和“more... than in any other country”就要立刻反应出这就是“领导者（leader）”的同义替换。

[D段] France is the pioneer in this sort of surveillance. More farmland is analysed by satellite there than in any other country, according to Infoterra (a subsidiary of EADS Astrium), the firm that is France's largest provider of such information, supplying data to companies such as Sevépi.

questions.question: a description of an innovation in satellite imaging which requires further study

analyses.content: 文中提到了“红边波段（Red-Edge band）”这一新技术，并明确指出需要“更多研究（More research）”来发挥其潜力。
这道题非常直接，只要把“innovation”对应到“Red-Edge band”，把“further study”对应到“more research”即可。

[F段] 'Our satellites are the first commercial satellites to include the Red-Edge band of the light spectrum, which is sensitive to changes in chlorophyll content. More research will be necessary to realise the full potential of the Red-Edge band.

questions.question: evidence of the cost effectiveness of using satellite technology in agriculture

analyses.content: [B段] The service usually costs less than US$15 per hectare for a handful of readings a year, and can increase yields by as much as 10%.
看到“cost effectiveness”，你必须在段落中找到关于“钱”和“收益”的具体数字对比。
段落末尾给出了具体的数据：每公顷成本不到15美元，却能增加高达10%的产量，这证明了投入少、产出高的性价比。

questions.question: Which TWO companies obtain information directly from satellites?

analyses.content: 文中提到 Infoterra 是法国最大的此类信息“供应商（provider）”，也就是直接把卫星分析的数据卖给别人。
你可能想选 Sevépi，但它只是“购买（purchases）”数据的合作社，相当于二道贩子或使用者，不是直接从卫星拿数据的源头。

[D段] More farmland is analysed by satellite there than in any other country, according to Infoterra (a subsidiary of EADS Astrium), the firm that is France's largest provider of such information, supplying data to companies such as Sevépi.

questions.question: Which TWO companies obtain information directly from satellites?

analyses.content: 原文直接称 RapidEye 为“卫星运营商（satellite operator）”，并引用他们的话说“我们的卫星（Our satellites）...”，身份确凿。
不要被 Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada 迷惑，它和 Sevépi 一样，明确说明了数据是“购买（purchases）”来的。

[E段] And according to RapidEye, a German satellite operator, insurance companies are also studying satellite data with a view to selling insurance policies... [F段] 'Our satellites are the first commercial satellites to include the Red-Edge band of the light spectrum...'

卫星是通过计算农田反射回来的“电磁辐射”总量来获取信息的。
题目问的是“测量什么”，原文中“calculating the amount of...”后面的内容就是答案，注意字数限制，填这两个词最准确。

由于题目说的是“谁相信（believes）”，你需要回原文找人名，并对应“reckons”或“says”等表达看法的动词。

[D段] Moreover, Henri Douche, head of Infoterra's agriculture sales in Toulouse, reckons the amount of monitored farmland will increase as weather patterns change and farmers can no longer rely on the past as a guide to the future. When confounded by the yield variations that these new weather patterns will bring, even farmers who are afraid of new technology will sign up, he says.
